# English words with punctuation next to them, typed correctly in the English
# layout.
#
# Used by tests/dev_tokens.rs and examples/measure_token_false_positives.rs to
# count how often automatic conversion would rewrite such a word as the same
# physical keys read in another layout: on the Russian layout "key." reads as
# "луню", on the Estonian layout "don't" reads as "donät" (audit findings C1-1
# and C1-2). The test file explains how to re-baseline the budget.
#
# Format: one token per line, lowercase letters a-z and the punctuation keys
# that print letters in the Russian or Estonian layout ([ ] ; ' , . and the
# shifted { } : " < >), at least two letters and one such key, sorted and
# unique. Between letters there is only an apostrophe or, in an abbreviation
# that ends with a period, a period. Lines that start with '#' are comments.
#
# Sources (public text only):
#   contractions   a fixed list of English contractions: don't, I've, they'll ...
#   abbreviations  a fixed list of abbreviations written with periods: e.g. ...
#   sentence ends  common short English words followed by a period or a comma:
#                  it. me. now, ...
#   prose          words with punctuation in this repository's English
#                  documentation (README.md and the tracked docs/*.md),
#                  lowercased; mistyped words quoted there as examples and an
#                  account name were left out
#   collisions     English dictionary words of three or more letters that read
#                  as a Russian dictionary word with the punctuation key after
#                  them (key. next. cream. rent; ...), found by scanning the
#                  bundled English and Russian word lists
#
# Snapshot taken on 2026-10-17 from the documentation at commit 7dea8f8.
